hints.title: Exploit Sorted Order
hints.text: Because nums is sorted, elements before index i are smaller and elements after index i are larger.

hints.title: Decompose Left and Right Sums
hints.text: Left contribution is i * nums[i] - prefix_sum, and right contribution is suffix_sum - (n - 1 - i) * nums[i].

hints.title: Compute Using Total Sum
hints.text: Maintain running prefix sum to derive suffix sum on the fly without extra arrays.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def getSumAbsoluteDifferences(self, nums: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        n = len(nums)
        total = sum(nums)
        pref = 0
        res = [0] * n
        for i, x in enumerate(nums):
            left_sum = i * x - pref
            right_sum = (total - pref - x) - (n - 1 - i) * x
            res[i] = left_sum + right_sum
            pref += x
        return res
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Computing pairwise absolute differences takes O(n^2) quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Prefix sums simplify algebraic expansion into O(n) time and O(n) output array.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should algebraically expand sum(|nums[i] - nums[j]|) using prefix and suffix totals.
